test_id_4.query: What rate codes should FQHCs use to bill for audio only telehealth?
test_id_4.answer:
FQHCs can bill the Prospective Payment System (PPS) rate code "4012" or "4013" for audio-only telehealth, depending on on-site presence. Additionally, for COVID-19 vaccine counseling provided via audio-only telehealth, FQHCs should bill the off-site rate code "4012" with CPT code "99429" appended with the GQ modifier.

1. Medicaid Update Special Edition Part Two: NYRx Pharmacy Benefit Transition Medicaid Update Volume 39 Number 1, page 11
   Published: 2/1/2023
   URL: https://health.ny.gov/health_care/medicaid/program/update/2023/docs/mu_no3_feb23_speced_pr.pdf
   Quote: "FQHCs can bill the Prospective Payment System (PPS) rate code “4012” or “4013”, depending on on-site presence"

2. New York State Medicaid Update February 2022 Volume 38 Number 2, page 6
   Published: 2/1/2022
   URL: https://health.ny.gov/health_care/medicaid/program/update/2022/docs/mu_no2_feb22_pr.pdf
   Quote: "FQHCs should bill the off-site rate code “4012” with CPT code “99429” appended with the GQ modifier to indicate the service was provided via audio-only (telephonic) telehealth."

3. New York State Medicaid Update November 2021 Volume 37 Number 13, page 6
   Published: 11/1/2021
   URL: https://health.ny.gov/health_care/medicaid/program/update/2021/docs/mu_no13_nov21_pr.pdf
   Quote: "FQHCs should bill the off-site rate code “4012” with CPT code “99429” appended with the GQ modifier to indicate the service was provided via audio-only (telephonic) telehealth."

test_id_8.query: What are the key components of the SCN program in the NYHER Waiver?
test_id_8.answer:
- The SCN program is part of the 1115 New York Health Equity Reform Waiver and aims to address health disparities by connecting Medicaid members to social services such as nutrition, housing, and transportation.
- Regional entities serve as lead entities for regional SCNs and develop networks of community-based organizations to deliver social care services.
- Members are screened using the CMS Accountable Health Communities Health-Related Social Needs Tool, and those with unmet needs receive navigation to state, federal, and local resources.
- Providers can connect patients to SCNs by providing referrals, connecting directly to the SCN platform or a Qualified Entity to submit screenings, or through other agreed-upon methods.

test_id_9.answer:
- Restricted recipients must obtain all care directly from their assigned providers or through a referral from them.
- The assigned Primary Care Provider (PCP) is responsible for coordinating care by issuing referrals for specialty services and non-emergency medical services when a specialist is required.
- Claims for restricted recipients will be denied if the assigned PCP is not included on the claim as the referring provider.
- Pharmacies are required to verify referrals with the assigned PCP if a prescription is written by a different provider.
- Opioid Treatment Program (OTP) services are fully exempt from these referral requirements.

An assigned primary care provider (PCP) is responsible for... coordinating care through referral to another medical provider for specialty services.

Claims submitted for a restricted recipient will be denied if information for the assigned PCP is not included on the claim as the referring provider.

test_id_10.query: what are the requirements for a referral for enrollment in the childrens waiver?
test_id_10.answer:
- A referral is appropriate when a parent, doctor, school, or service provider identifies a child or youth as potentially needing Home and Community Based Services (HCBS).
- Children who are not already enrolled in Medicaid must be referred to the Children and Youth Evaluation Services (C-YES) to determine eligibility and assist with the Medicaid application.
- A child should not be enrolled in the waiver if State Plan or Community First Choice Option (CFCO) services alone meet their needs, unless the child is only eligible for Medicaid under the "Family of One" criteria.
